header:
Date: 2026-09-17
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Jasper Lowe (Montclair CTO), Dr. Nina Patel (Montclair Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Montclair Infra), Ava Kim (Montclair SRE)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on latency/throughput delta versus customer baseline. Redwood presented updated bench runs with routing and quantization tweaks. Customer asked clarifying Qs about SSO/KMS, dedicated slot guarantees, and fallback behavior. Agreement to run an additional 95th percentile test with 128-token context and share traffic traces for parity testing.
topics: routing playbook and fallback to model variants
quantization and batch sizing impact on p99
security requirements: SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick agenda — we'll run through the latest bench results, call out the latency deltas versus your incumbent, and propose a small tuning run. Priya and I will own the follow ups.
[00:18] Jasper Lowe: Sounds good. we had the team look at last week's numbers and low level there was a big p99 spike on tail on the first page. curious what changed in your routing.
[00:34] Priya Desai: yeah great question. so we adjusted the routing policy to prefer the low-latency pool for calls under 100ms SLO and left the cost-optimized pool for the rest. also enabled prefix KV cache for repeated prompts — sometimes transcribed as K V cache in notes — that shaved off about 8 to 12 ms median on sample flows.
[00:52] Dr. Nina Patel: when you say low-latency pool is that Dedicated or Hosted? our compliance team wants to know the isolation guarantees.
[01:05] Priya Desai: it's Hosted low-latency instance group for the pilot, not Dedicated. we can move to Dedicated slots if we need strict isolation and throughput reservation. the configuration we ran last night was a quantized fp16 path with a tuned batch size of 4, plus the cache.
[01:27] Marco Ruiz: what was the context window? our baseline runs use 128 tokens on average, we want apples to apples.
[01:34] Priya Desai: good catch — last run used 64 tokens, which explains some of the delta. we'll re-run at 128 tokens for 95th and 99th percentiles, that's on the action items.
[01:44] Ava Kim: also curious about your fallback policy. if the low-latency pool fills up do requests fall back to a quantized variant with slightly lower quality? we've seen LexoCloud do a sudden drop and it's not acceptable for critical flows.
[02:00] Ethan Park: yes. our routing playbook does an automatic fallback to a compatible model variant — typically a lower-precision quantized build — but we can set hard limits and circuit-breakers to avoid silent quality drops. we also have canary routing so a small percentage is routed to the fallback first.
[02:20] Jasper Lowe: can you show the plot comparing p95/p99 vs our incumbent?
[02:27] Priya Desai: scrolling share — ok the slide here (shared) shows median/p95/p99 across three load tiers. median's pretty close, p95 is within 10-12% and p99 we currently sit about 18-25% higher than your baseline on the 64-token run. but when we enabled prefix caching and bumped batch size the p95 improved notably.
[02:54] Dr. Nina Patel: 18-25% at p99 is non-trivial; what's the root cause walk-through? is it batching, GC, or kernel selection?
[03:06] Priya Desai: it's mostly headroom exhaustion on the low-latency pool when traffic bursts; the scheduler then moves to a slightly different kernel path and the KV cache misses amplify tail. also the bigger variable is our model quantization profile — some ops hit slower kernels in fp16 for certain sequence lengths.
[03:29] Liam O'Connor: quick note — transcription sometimes shows Redwood Privet instead of Private in our notes, just to flag that for the document.
[03:36] Marco Ruiz: for the 128-token run, are you going to use the same batch policy? our traffic's spiky so we want smaller batches to preserve latency.
[03:44] Priya Desai: we'll use dynamic batching with a smaller max batch cap — something like max batch 6 and aggressive flush at 30ms so spikes don't accumulate. that should trade a bit of throughput for lower tail.
[04:01] Jasper Lowe: what's our unit cost delta if you reduce batching like that? economics is part of the decision.
[04:07] Ethan Park: rough math — throughput goes down maybe 6-9% in tokens/sec on that model, and unit cost goes up accordingly. we'll send a delta sheet showing cost per 1M tokens under both batch policies.
[04:21] Dr. Nina Patel: on security, we need KMS integration for keys and SOC 2 evidence. also SSO with our Okta identity.
[04:31] Ethan Park: yes we support customer-managed KMS, HSM option in Private deployments, and we have an Okta SAML flow. we'll attach the SOC 2 type 2 report and the audit-log spec after the call.
[04:45] Ava Kim: in terms of observability, can you export token-level traces and per-token timing? that's how we correlate user-facing latency to model steps.
[04:55] Priya Desai: yep we can include token timing and the per-route breakdown. note that very fine-grained traces add a bit of overhead so we usually snapshot a sample window.
[05:08] Jasper Lowe: ok let's talk timeline, can you get the 128-token p99 run by early next week? we have an internal decision sync on Thursday.
[05:15] Priya Desai: yes — we'll run overnight and aim to share results and raw bench scripts by Tuesday/Wednesday.
[05:23] Marco Ruiz: we'll also upload a 24h p99 traffic trace from production, maybe scrubbed for PHI, by Monday.
[05:30] Ethan Park: perfect. any other blockers?
[05:33] Dr. Nina Patel: curious about cold-start behavior for rare queries. our dataset has long tail prompts, does Redwood warm KV cache across model variants?
[05:44] Priya Desai: we warm actively for frequent prefixes when using the prefix cache, and we can prepopulate the KV cache during off-peak with a warm-up job. for rare queries we accept some cold-starts but the routing prefers warmed instances.
[05:58] Jasper Lowe: earlier you mentioned a canary percent. what are reasonable defaults?
[06:04] Priya Desai: typical is 5% canary, ramp to 25% depending on stability signals. we also have automatic rollback on error or latency regressions.
[06:15] Ava Kim: on the audit side, we need a sample of the console's per-route latency dashboard. can you export a PDF?
[06:22] Liam O'Connor: yes we'll export a dashboard snapshot and a CSV with the raw metrics.
[06:27] Marco Ruiz: any gotchas with VPC peering if we later move to Private?
[06:32] Ethan Park: it's straightforward but we should schedule a security deep dive. some customers do a private control plane with customer-managed networking; that's more of a timeline and procurement discussion.
[06:44] Dr. Nina Patel: last thing — does Redwood offer token-level cost attribution in the console? we want to map cost to product route.
[06:52] Priya Desai: yes per-route and per-token cost breakdown is available. we can attach an example export.
[06:58] Jasper Lowe: ok recap and next steps?
[07:02] Ethan Park: recap: Redwood to re-run bench at 128 tokens (Priya) and share 95th/99th plots and raw scripts; customer to provide 24h traffic trace (Marco); Ethan to send pricing delta for Dedicated/burst; schedule security deep dive if latency parity looks good.
[07:19] Dr. Nina Patel: that's it from us, thanks.
[07:22] Ethan Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and propose times for the security call.
[07:28] (recording stopped)
